title: Passenger boat bound for Turtle Islands drifts without fuel for six days; 121 rescued
summary: A passenger vessel sailing from Zamboanga City to Turtle Islands, Tawi-Tawi with 106 passengers and 15 crew had engine trouble near Pangutaran Island on 8 January 2025, broke down again and drifted without fuel or signal. Fishermen spotted it and the Navy reached it about 5.4 nautical miles west of Siklangkalong Island on Tuesday, 14 January 2025; everyone was taken to Turtle Islands and the boat towed to Taja Island. Manila Bulletin named it the M/L J Sayang 1.

title: M/L Bangsata sinks in rough seas 17 nautical miles off Turtle Islands; all 32 aboard rescued
summary: The wooden-hulled M/L Bangsata, which left Turtle Islands for South Ubian, Tawi-Tawi at about 1:45 a.m. on Sunday, 16 March 2025 with 32 people, sank in rough seas at about 6 a.m. some 17 nautical miles southeast of the Turtle Islands. Survivors clung to debris until a passing tanker raised the alarm; the Navy’s BRP Jose Loor Sr. rescued 26 about 16 hours later and a Malaysian vessel picked up the other 6.

title: M/L Nurdia drifts with a broken rudder east of Taganak Island; Navy rescues 30
summary: The motor launch M/L Nurdia, with 30 passengers and crew including a pregnant woman, two senior citizens and five children, was found drifting with a broken rudder about 46 nautical miles east of Taganak Island, Turtle Islands, Tawi-Tawi on the night of Friday, 16 January 2026. A Navy patrol craft on routine patrol spotted its flashing light and landed everyone at Taganak port by 4:45 a.m. Saturday.

title: M/L Sitti Nur overturns in big waves between Simunul and Bongao; all 12 aboard rescued
summary: The old wooden M/L Sitti Nur, sailing from Manuk Mangkaw seaport in Simunul to Bongao pier, Tawi-Tawi, was overturned by big waves at the sea border of the two towns on Monday, 19 January 2026. All 12 passengers and crew could swim and clung to the upturned hull until responders reached them; the boat carried no life jackets. They were taken to the Datu Halun Sakilan Memorial Hospital in Bongao for examination.

title: Ferry MV Trisha Kerstin 3 sinks off Baluk-Baluk Island; 65 dead, 14 missing by 22 February
summary: The Aleson Shipping Lines ferry MV Trisha Kerstin 3 sank past midnight on Monday, 26 January 2026 off Baluk-Baluk Island, Hadji Muhtamad, Basilan with more than 340 people aboard. The Coast Guard counted 293 rescued; the toll rose as bodies were recovered, to 57 by 16 February, 62 by 18 February and 65 dead with 14 missing by 22 February 2026.

title: MV Lady Mary Joy 3 burns off Baluk-Baluk Island; 33 dead once the last missing passenger was found
summary: The passenger ferry MV Lady Mary Joy 3 caught fire late on Wednesday, 29 March 2023 off Baluk-Baluk Island, Hadji Muhtamad, Basilan. The Coast Guard’s toll reached 31 on 30 March and 33 on 13 April 2023, when the body of the last missing passenger, recovered on 11 April, was counted; faulty wiring was the suspected cause.
